Gluten is a protein complex primarily found in wheat, barley, and rye, composed of glutenin and gliadin proteins. It provides dough with its essential viscoelastic properties, enabling bread to rise and develop its characteristic chewiness, which is manipulated in baking through flour choice and kneading techniques. Industrially, gluten is processed into a powder and added to foods to enhance texture and protein content, and it serves as the base for meat alternatives like seitan. Beyond food, gluten can act as a stabilizing agent in products like ice cream and ketchup. For a subset of the population, however, gluten triggers adverse immune responses, leading to conditions like celiac disease and necessitating a gluten-free diet.
